extraction_metadata.notes: Ermelinda Damko's 'Data-Rich, Insight-Poor' series entry XXXVII — a recomputed statistical analysis of the GPCR structural corpus from GPCRdb. The central finding is a methodological fingerprint: cryo-EM produces 91% active-state structures because single-particle alignment requires mass and asymmetry, and the G protein provides both. This is arguably the round's most precise OSIRIS match — the G protein literally functions as the fiducial marker that makes the imaging possible.

title: The G protein was doing the alignment — why the cryo-EM GPCR corpus is 91% active-state
subtitle_or_tagline: Data-Rich, Insight-Poor XXXVII — the coverage map that looks like scientific priorities but is actually a residue of image processing
topic: A recomputed analysis of the GPCR structural corpus (GPCRdb export through end-2024) showing that of 1,210 cryo-EM GPCR structures only ~9% are inactive-state, versus ~71% inactive among 504 X-ray structures. The cause is not conceptual but physical: single-particle alignment needs mass and asymmetry, and an agonist-bound GPCR plus its heterotrimeric G protein (~40 kDa receptor + rigidly-coupled large, lopsided effector) provides both, while an antagonist-bound receptor's closed intracellular face provides neither. The consequence: 218 of 287 non-olfactory class A receptors have never been seen in the conformation most of their antagonists stabilize, against a pharmacopoeia where ~44% of approved GPCR drugs are antagonists. The field's surrogate strategies (BRIL fusions, Legobodies, NabFab, PGS fusions, ICL3 grafts) each add expression and purification burden plus unstated linker-screening costs.

architecture.data_flow: receptor + (G protein OR surrogate fiducial) -> cryo-EM single-particle alignment -> 3D reconstruction -> state-biased structural corpus

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Express receptor (with or without fusion surrogate)
Step 2 - Bind agonist + G protein (easy alignment) or antagonist alone (alignment-starved)
Step 4 - Align particles — the fiducial determines whether orientations resolve
Step 5 - Deposit structure; corpus statistics accumulate the active-state bias
key_claims: Of 1,210 cryo-EM GPCR structures only ~9% are inactive-state; X-ray shows ~71% inactive of 504
Alignment requires mass and asymmetry — the G protein supplies both, antagonist-bound receptors supply neither
218 of 287 non-olfactory class A receptors have no inactive-state structure
Only 36 GPCRs of any class are solved in both activation states
~44% of approved GPCR-directed drugs are antagonists — the corpus does not describe the pharmacopoeia
Surrogate fiducial strategies (BRIL fusions, nanobodies, Legobodies) work but add multi-protein expression burden and unbounded linker screening
caveats_or_warnings: Absolute totals will drift as GPCRdb updates; the ratios carry the argument
Analysis covers class A non-olfactory receptors; other classes not fully censused

osiris_connection: This is the most literal OSIRIS confirmation the monitoring has surfaced: the G protein IS the fiducial marker. OSIRIS's fiducial-marker concept (astronomy: a reference of known geometry calibrates the imaging pipeline; biology: gpcr-fiducial-markers card) states that imaging a small, symmetric object is bound-limited by the fiducial you can attach. Damko's recomputed statistics prove it at corpus scale — the 91% active-state bias is not a scientific priority but a fiducial constraint: no fiducial, no alignment, no structure. The surrogate-fiducial zoo (BRIL, NabFab, Legobodies) is the field hand-engineering what OSIRIS formalizes: every imaging act needs a bounded reference, and the displacement you can resolve (Δx) is set by the fiducial's rigidity (L) and size (c). The 218 unsolved inactive states are the unbounded regime — no fiducial, no certificate.
